messages:
maria: Heads up — during the midnight rollout I see a cascade of ArgoCD prune failures targeting edge-eu-2-gpu. Apps are stuck in PrunePending and the repo-server is returning 429s.

maria: excerpt from repo-server log: ```ERROR repo-server request failed: rate limited by controller (429) path=/api/v1/repo/xxxx status=429```

argocd-bot: prune-wave 22 triggered: 120 apps -> 3s/req -> 429 rate limit observed

aj: hmm. edge clusters often have stricter networkpolicies — could be repo-server -> cluster API latency, or we spike GitOps fanout causing controller to hit request rate limits.

sven: I also noticed terraform drift on the LB healthcheck on that VPC yesterday — idle timeout was reverted to 60s which killed long-lived connections to some nodes. Might be correlated.

kevin: quick checks: `kubectl -n argocd logs deploy/argocd-repo-server --since=15m` and `kubectl -n kube-system get events --field-selector type=Warning` on the edge cluster. Can someone paste results?

maria: pasted event snippet: ```Warning FailedCreate pod "gpu-provisioner" failed to create: NetworkPolicy blocked ingress from argocd-repo-server IP range```

jen: that explains the pruning stalls — repo-server cannot reach the cluster to perform deletes so it queues and retries. ArgoCD then starts throttling with 429s.

aj: short-term mitigation: reduce prune fanout so repo-server doesn't burst. In ArgoCD we can set `- --app-resync-limit=5` for repo-server or lower `sync.parallelism` in the app-of-apps. Also consider temporarily scaling repo-server replicas to 3.

sven: longer-term: fix the NetworkPolicy and Terraform drift. I found a revert in the infra repo: terraform/aws/lb.tf was changed by CI to set `idle_timeout = 60` accidentally. See PR #4123. We should pin it back to 360 and add a policy test.

kevin: proposed action list: 1) patch networkpolicy to allow argocd repo CIDR -> `kubectl patch netpol allowed-argocd -n infra --patch '...yaml...'` 2) scale repo-server deployment 3) apply a hotfix to app-of-apps `spec.syncOptions: - Replace=true` to reduce pruning concurrency temporarily

maria: I'm going to apply a targeted allow-rule and scale repo-server now. Will post results.

deploy-bot: running: `kubectl -n argocd scale deploy/argocd-repo-server --replicas=3` (initiated by maria)

maria: scaled to 3. Patch applied: `kubectl apply -f allow-argocd-egress.yaml -n infra`.

maria: within 2m prune wave started clearing backlog, many apps progressed to PruneInProgress then Synced. No more immediate 429s.

aj: great. We still need to address root causes: terraform drift + rate-limiting defaults in ArgoCD. Suggest two PRs: (A) infra: revert LB idle timeout + add terraform test; (B) argocd-config: set `repo-server.reconnectTimeout` and add `--repo-server-concurrency` lower default for edge clusters.

jen: also consider sharding the app-of-apps for edge clusters so each region's app-of-apps handles a smaller fanout. That prevents single large prune waves.

sven: cost note — scaling repo-server temporarily and re-provisioning GPU nodes increases short-term cost but avoids failed rollouts. Estimate ~<$100/day for the last 4 hours spike.

kevin: I'll open the two PRs now. tagging @infra-oncall for review and @security for networkpolicy exception signoff.

maria: thanks. One follow-up: can we add an ArgoCD health check in infra CI that runs `argocd app list --server` to ensure repo-server can access cluster APIs after infra changes? That would catch regressions earlier.

aj: yes — add a post-apply smoke test that queries cluster API from the repo-server pod and verifies netpol connectivity and LB healthcheck response.

maria: ok creating a small runbook for oncall: steps to scale repo-server, patch netpol, find drift PRs, and rollback if needed. Will drop runbook link here once done. :memo:

argocd-bot: incident resolved (partial) — prune backlog drained, monitoring on for 2h.

kevin: PRs opened: infra#4135 revert lb.tf, argocd#842 add concurrency flags. Adding tests and deps.

jen: good postmortem candidate if this repeats — note: networkpolicy + terraform reverts + app-of-apps fanout.

maria: runbook attached: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/argocd-prune-edge (private link)

aj: will follow up tomorrow to plan sharding rollout and CI smoke tests. Closing for now. :white_check_mark:
